merged.title: feat(port): route GPU work through the render graph
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Route Vulkan draws, dispatches, transfers and submission through declared graph work. Validate resource ownership, image subresources, buffer ranges and pipeline bindings before recording work.

- Preserve the Vulkan optimizations from develop. Defer optional pipeline upgrades during gameplay and retain their keys for prewarming at a later load.

## Verification

- Windows RAC1 NTSC release build.
- 22 Vulkan render equivalence and render graph checks with synchronization validation enabled. Both image comparison shards passed.

merged.title: fix(mods): close your own world-writable mod folders instead of refusing
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on a Steam Deck the plugins folder was writable by all (a program started from Steam may run with umask 0), so the port refused every native mod.

**After:** a file or folder of your own that all may write in is closed to others (`chmod o-w`) and the mod loads. Only a library or folder owned by another user than you and root is refused.

**How:** `open_to_others` in `mod_library.cpp` checks the owner first, then closes your own world-writable items. `docs/port/MODS.md` updated.

**Tested:** `mod_loader_test`: own world-writable file and folder get closed and load, another owner's file or folder is refused, a link is followed; `ctest -R mod_loader` passes.

merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:

Switching between Games and Mods on Android made buttons flicker for a few frames. Mods came in empty and its lists, notice, toolbar and buttons popped in during the slide; on Games the last save line and Play's "Continue" came a moment after the shelf. merged.title: fix(hdr): keep SDR hue where SDR shows a flame white
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before

With SDR Hue at 100%, a flame's core turned red inside a yellow flame (thruster pack, ship engines). Where every channel is past white, SDR shows white, which has no hue, so those pixels fell back to HDR's red.

## After

SDR Hue keeps the hue SDR gave the pixel just before it turned white, so the flame stays yellow to its core with no cut-off. SDR Chrominance still uses the real SDR pixel. With default settings nothing changes.

## How

- `hdr::sdr_hue_of`: the pixel scaled down until its lowest channel is at 0.8, then clipped at white. `apply_look` takes its hue from that.
- Same in `hdr_encode.comp`.

## Tested

- `hdr` (new test: a flame added up from orange to white, the hue moves smoothly and stays yellow) and `vulkan_hdr` (GPU against CPU) pass; conventions pass.
- Not checked on a real HDR screen.

merged.title: fix(launcher): smooth tab slides and less background work
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on Android the Games wave vanished and popped back during tab slides, buttons flickered, a tap on Games waited ~170 ms before sliding, and fast tab switching kept the CPU busy (fans). Every tab switch re-hashed the Enhanced bake files (up to 200 ms per call, also on desktop).

**After:**
- A still 2D copy of the wave shows while a page slides; the wave's clock waits too, so it goes on from the same picture.
- The slide waits only for pending images to load (max 120 ms), not decode.
- Bake file hashes are cached by size + mtime; `sha2` is optimized in debug builds (the APK).
- Idle Games: wave drops to 30 fps; far discs are hidden and their animations paused.

**Tested:** `yarn verify`, headless frame diffs, and on an Ayn Odin 3: Games tap to slide 169 -> 49 ms, longest frame gap 175 -> 50 ms, no wave jump (6/6 slides), Rust threads 208% -> 23% at 4 switches/s. Desktop (Windows, 1.0.2): hashing was the only shared issue and is fixed by the cache.

merged.title: fix(rac1): run each level's own sky routine
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on a level, the frame draw's C called the executable's sky routine (the title's stars). On the PS2, each level's copy of the frame draw calls the level's own sky routine. So the port reseeded `rand()` once, called it about 250 more times a frame (the same `rand()` the Decoy and Morph-o-Ray use), wrote 256 stars to address 0, and Novalis's clouds stood still.

**After:** on a level, `Transition_DrawSky` calls where the level's copy of the frame draw calls. The title still runs the executable's C.

**How:** a wrap of `Transition_DrawSky` (`rac1/host/sky.c`, NTSC and PAL rows in libraries.tsv) and `openrac_level_call` in the runtime: it reads the level copy's own `jal` at the place of the executable's. NTSC-J and PAL v1 leave it out (RAC1_OMIT) until checked. No decomp C changed.

**Tested (NTSC, container):**
- Novalis: `rand()` calls a frame 466 -> 227; the sky record matches PCSX2 byte for byte (star count 0); bytes written at 0..0x2400: 7367 -> 0; clouds drift as on PCSX2.

merged.title: fix(port): ignore faults other modules catch on Windows
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Fixes T-19: rac1 crashes on Windows when a Discord screen share starts.

**Before:** The crash handler is a vectored handler, so it sees every first-chance fault in the process. RivaTuner (RTSSHooks64.dll, woken by the screen share) probes a pointer with `IsBadReadPtr(0xFFFF...)` and catches the fault itself. Our handler saw it first and ended the game ("read at host address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF").

**After:** The game keeps running. Real crashes are still reported.

**How:**
- The vectored handler reports a fault at once only in our own code: the .exe, the disc part and native mods (they never catch a fault). `mods::library::open/close` register and drop the library.
- A fault in any other library (overlay, driver) goes on to its own handler. If nobody catches it, the unhandled filter reports it with the same read/write/execute details.

**Tested:**

**After:** The game keeps running. Real crashes are still reported.

**How:**
- The vectored handler reports a fault at once only in our own code: the .exe, the disc part and native mods (they never catch a fault). `mods::library::open/close` register and drop the library.
- A fault in any other library (overlay, driver) goes on to its own handler. If nobody catches it, the unhandled filter reports it with the same read/write/execute details.

**Tested:**
- Small Windows test under Wine (mingw build of `crash.cpp`): the old code dies on a foreign `IsBadReadPtr(-1)`, the new code goes on. Faul

## What

Matches 2 functions: the PAL and USA v2.00 copies of `func_002DC3C8`, the timed text page controller matched for USA v1.01 in #451.
